requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I found no gap in `requirements.ci.span`. Every obligation has code that carries it out and a test that runs that code.

**Reachability.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` carries the `{impl}` reference. It calls `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs`, which calls `colon_fence`, `overlaps_protected` and `code_block_ranges`. It also calls `without_options` and `.trim()`. The code that carries out the obligations is therefore reachable from the marked item, and none of it needs its own reference. `definition_blocks` is itself marked for `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`.

**Obligations, code and tests:**
- **Opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`.**
  - Code: `colon_fence` requires `length >= 3`. `definition_blocks` then strips the `{req}` prefix directly after the colons. It requires whitespace and a valid name after the prefix, so `:::{req}ready` and `::: {req} ready` are rejected.
  - Test: `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]` asserts that `::{req}`, `::: {req}` and `:::{req}ready` yield no blocks.
- **Closing fence has at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else but whitespace.**
  - Code: the close search in `definition_blocks` requires `count >= fence_length && suffix.trim().is_empty()`. Candidate lines inside code blocks are skipped by `overlaps_protected`.
  - Tests: `:::foo` does not close and `::: ` does, in the `closing_fences_allow…` test. A `::::` block containing a nested `:::{note}` is covered by `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive`. A `:::` inside a code fence is covered by `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]`.
- **Fences MAY be indented up to three spaces; four or more MUST NOT be a fence.**
  - Code: `colon_fence` returns `None` when the indent is greater than 3.
  - Test: the `closing_fences_allow…` test checks a three-space opening and closing pair. It also checks that a four-space opening yields no block and that a four-space closing line leaves the block unclosed.
- **Body is all Markdown between the fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams and blank lines.**
  - Code: `body_start` is the start of the line after the opening fence and `body_end` is the start of the closing fence line. `collect_definitions` builds the text from that range through `without_options`, which only removes option lines.
  - Tests: `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` covers a body with a code block, ATX and setext headings, and blank lines. `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` covers a fenced example in the body.
- **Body MUST NOT include text after the closing fence.**
  - Code: `body_end` stops at the closing fence line.
  - Tests: the "Outside the requirement." text is excluded in `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text`. `Outside.` stays outside the block in the `::::` test.
- **Leading and trailing whitespace is excluded when comparing the body with evidence.**
  - Code: `.trim()` in `collect_definitions`.
  - Test: `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace]`.
- **Unclosed fence.** The text does not name this case. It is handled by `closed = false` with an error from `collect_definitions`, and `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` tests it.

Every test carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.ci.span`. I found no unspecified behavior.
